grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain kitchen staple: kippers, cabbage, flour, eggs, milk, cheddar, butter and mustard.

supermarket.reason: Kipper fillets, Savoy cabbage and the baking staples are all everyday items at Tesco at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: A muffin tin, frying pan and mixing bowl are common household kit, and simple mix-and-bake muffins suit a beginner.

works.reason: 250g self-raising flour, 2 eggs and 200ml milk, plus the buttery cabbage, make a sensible batter for 12 savoury muffins; 20 minutes at 200°C cooks the flaked kipper through, and the kipper and cheese give enough salt.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is tight but believable for shredding a quarter cabbage, flaking two kippers, grating cheese and filling the tin, and the 20-minute bake matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme and pepper, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Savoy cabbage leads the title and runs through every muffin, which suits a warm baked snack in mid-February.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: The muffins combine oily fish, egg, cheese and greens in a filling savoury snack rather than refined starch alone.
